**Daniel Houser** (born November 1973) is an English writer and producer.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-2) He is one of the co-founders of Rockstar Games alongside his brother Sam Houser. He served as the head writer and vice president of creativity[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-NYT-4) until his resignation in 2020. He founded [Absurd Ventures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absurd_Ventures "Absurd Ventures") in 2021, creating new [intellectual properties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_properties "Intellectual properties") across several mediums. He is a writer for the _American Caper_ comic book series for Absurd Ventures alongside [Lazlow Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazlow_Jones "Lazlow Jones").

Prior to his departure from the company, Houser was regarded as the primary creative driving force behind much of Rockstar's output.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Inverse-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-screenrant-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-arstechnica-7) First serving as the sole writer for _[Grand Theft Auto: London 1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand\_Theft\_Auto:\_London\_1969 "Grand Theft Auto: London 1969")_ (1997), he went on to become the lead writer and creative director for most titles in the _[Grand Theft Auto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand\_Theft\_Auto "Grand Theft Auto")_ series,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-NYT-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-theguardian-hill-8)_[Red Dead Redemption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_Dead\_Redemption "Red Dead Redemption")_ (2010) and _[Red Dead Redemption 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_Dead\_Redemption\_2 "Red Dead Redemption 2")_ (2018), _[Bully](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bully\_(video\_game) "Bully (video game)")_ (2006), _[Midnight Club: Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Club:\_Los\_Angeles "Midnight Club: Los Angeles")_ (2008), and _[Max Payne 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max\_Payne\_3 "Max Payne 3")_ (2012).

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dan_Houser&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Daniel Houser was born in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-9) in November 1973,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-VGC_Absurd-1) the son of actress [Geraldine Moffat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geraldine_Moffat "Geraldine Moffat") and solicitor and saxophonist Walter Houser (1934–2025).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Meet_the_brains-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-12) He was educated at [St Paul's School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Paul's_School,_London "St Paul's School, London") before matriculating in 1993 at [Christ Church, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christ_Church,_Oxford "Christ Church, Oxford"), where he read geography.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-theguardian-hill-8)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-13) Despite wanting to be musicians, both Houser and his brother Sam (alongside whom he would later co-found Rockstar Games) had a fascination with storytelling from a young age. Growing up near a video library in London, they watched many American crime and cult films and [Spaghetti Westerns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaghetti_Western "Spaghetti Western"). Houser has stated that he is a fan of the film _[The Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Warriors\_(film) "The Warriors (film)")_;[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-NYT2-14) Rockstar later released a [video game adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Warriors_(video_game) "The Warriors (video game)") of the film in 2005.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-NYT2-14)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dan_Houser&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early work and Rockstar Games

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dan_Houser&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early work and Rockstar Games")]

In 1995, Houser got a part-time job at [BMG Interactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMG_Interactive "BMG Interactive") testing [CD-ROMs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CD-ROM "CD-ROM"); he became a full-time employee until 1996.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Meet_the_brains-10)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-15) Dan and Sam later became interested in a video game being developed by [DMA Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DMA_Design "DMA Design") called _Race'n'Chase_ after getting a preview of the game. The Housers signed _Race'n'Chase_ to BMG Interactive as the publisher and changed the name of the game to _[Grand Theft Auto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand\_Theft\_Auto\_(video\_game) "Grand Theft Auto (video game)")_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-16) Following the sale of BMG Interactive to [Take-Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take-Two "Take-Two") in 1998, Houser and his brother moved with the company to New York, where they founded Rockstar Games.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Meet_the_brains-10) He has cited the 3D _[Mario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario\_(franchise) "Mario (franchise)")_ and _[Zelda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda "The Legend of Zelda")_ games on the [Nintendo 64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_64 "Nintendo 64") as influences on his work.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-17)

Houser has been credited as a writer for twelve _Grand Theft Auto_ titles and a producer for six.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-18) Despite the high profile of the _Grand Theft Auto_ series, Houser and his brother have shied away from the celebrity spotlight, preferring to focus on the Rockstar Games brand rather than giving any one person the credit for the games' success.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-19) In 2009, both Dan and Sam Houser appeared in [_Time_ magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")'s [100 most influential people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100") of 2009 list.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-20)

Houser and his brother were inducted into the [Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Interactive_Arts_&_Sciences "Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences")'s Hall of Fame in 2014.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-21)

### Departure from Rockstar and founding of Absurd Ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dan_Houser&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Departure from Rockstar and founding of Absurd Ventures")]

In February 2020, Rockstar Games's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, announced Houser's resignation from Rockstar Games. He left Rockstar on 11 March 2020, following an extended break in 2019.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-23) In February 2021, Houser registered two companies in [Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware "Delaware"): [Absurd Ventures LLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absurd_Ventures_LLC "Absurd Ventures LLC") and Absurd Ventures in Games LLC, the latter with a UK-based subsidiary in [Altrincham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altrincham "Altrincham"). Houser is listed as the company's producer and creative director.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-VGC_Absurd-1) In June 2023, Houser officially announced his involvement in the studio, which he said will "create new universes" in video games, books, graphic novels, scripted podcasts, live-action, and animation.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-24)

In November 2023, it was revealed that [Lazlow Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazlow_Jones "Lazlow Jones") and Michael Unsworth had joined the company as executive producer and head of story, respectively.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-25) The company also announced its first projects: a graphic novel called _American Caper_ and an audio series called _A Better Paradise_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-26) In September 2024, Absurd Ventures announced the formation of Absurd Marin, made up of about 20 developers from [Ascendant Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascendant_Studios "Ascendant Studios"), developers of _[Immortals of Aveum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immortals\_of\_Aveum "Immortals of Aveum")_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-27)

In January 2025, Absurd Ventures released the logo and lineup of characters for the 'Absurdaverse', a new universe with animation and a "story-driven action-comedy adventure game."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-29)

Houser has novelised _A Better Paradise_ with the first volume published on October 14, 2025 accompanied by an audiobook edition on Audible.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-30)

In November 2025, Absurd Ventures began releasing a monthly comic book series titled _American Caper_, published by [Dark Horse Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_Horse_Comics "Dark Horse Comics"), with the first trade paperback collection scheduled for release in June 2026. [[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-31) A French edition was announced by publisher Urban Comics and scheduled for release in September 2026. [[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-32)

### Other work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dan_Houser&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Other work")]

By September 2022, Houser joined the advisory board of Revolving Games, a [blockchain game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain_game "Blockchain game") studio, after investing in a US$13.2 million funding round for the company;[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-VGC_Revolving-33) He met co-founder Saad Zaeem some years earlier to explore ideas, but they ultimately chose different projects, leading Houser to become an adviser and investor instead.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-VentureBeat_Revolving-34)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dan_Houser&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Houser is married to entrepreneur Krystyna Jakubiak.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Variety_LA-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Architectural_Digest-37) They previously lived in [Truman Capote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truman_Capote "Truman Capote")'s former home in the [Brooklyn Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Heights "Brooklyn Heights") neighborhood of New York City, which they purchased for US$12.5 million, the most expensive home sale in Brooklyn's history.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-40) In 2020, they purchased [Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien")'s former home in the [Brentwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brentwood,_Los_Angeles "Brentwood, Los Angeles") neighborhood of Los Angeles.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Variety_LA-36) They have three children and own a holiday lodge along [Saranac Lake, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saranac_Lake,_New_York "Saranac Lake, New York"), built in the 1920s.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Architectural_Digest-37) Houser holds both British and American citizenship.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-VGC_Absurd-1) Houser, Sam, and their wives were directors of the Houser Foundation Inc. in New York,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Foundation-41) founded in 2008; it was renamed the Krystyna and Dan Houser Foundation in 2024.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-42) Houser serves on the boards of the [Rainforest Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainforest_Alliance "Rainforest Alliance")[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-43) and [Brooklyn Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Museum "Brooklyn Museum").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-44)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Foundation-41)

**Daniel Houser** (born November 1973) is an English writer and producer.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-2) He is one of the co-founders of Rockstar Games alongside his brother Sam Houser. He served as the head writer and vice president of creativity[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-NYT-4) until his resignation in 2020. He founded [Absurd Ventures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absurd_Ventures "Absurd Ventures") in 2021, creating new [intellectual properties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_properties "Intellectual properties") across several mediums. He is a writer for the _American Caper_ comic book series for Absurd Ventures alongside [Lazlow Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazlow_Jones "Lazlow Jones").

Prior to his departure from the company, Houser was regarded as the primary creative driving force behind much of Rockstar's output.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Inverse-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-screenrant-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-arstechnica-7) First serving as the sole writer for _[Grand Theft Auto: London 1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand\_Theft\_Auto:\_London\_1969 "Grand Theft Auto: London 1969")_ (1997), he went on to become the lead writer and creative director for most titles in the _[Grand Theft Auto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand\_Theft\_Auto "Grand Theft Auto")_ series,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-NYT-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-theguardian-hill-8)_[Red Dead Redemption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_Dead\_Redemption "Red Dead Redemption")_ (2010) and _[Red Dead Redemption 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red\_Dead\_Redemption\_2 "Red Dead Redemption 2")_ (2018), _[Bully](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bully\_(video\_game) "Bully (video game)")_ (2006), _[Midnight Club: Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Club:\_Los\_Angeles "Midnight Club: Los Angeles")_ (2008), and _[Max Payne 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max\_Payne\_3 "Max Payne 3")_ (2012).

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dan_Houser&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Daniel Houser was born in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-9) in November 1973,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-VGC_Absurd-1) the son of actress [Geraldine Moffat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geraldine_Moffat "Geraldine Moffat") and solicitor and saxophonist Walter Houser (1934–2025).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Meet_the_brains-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-12) He was educated at [St Paul's School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Paul's_School,_London "St Paul's School, London") before matriculating in 1993 at [Christ Church, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christ_Church,_Oxford "Christ Church, Oxford"), where he read geography.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-theguardian-hill-8)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-13) Despite wanting to be musicians, both Houser and his brother Sam (alongside whom he would later co-found Rockstar Games) had a fascination with storytelling from a young age. Growing up near a video library in London, they watched many American crime and cult films and [Spaghetti Westerns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaghetti_Western "Spaghetti Western"). Houser has stated that he is a fan of the film _[The Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Warriors\_(film) "The Warriors (film)")_;[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-NYT2-14) Rockstar later released a [video game adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Warriors_(video_game) "The Warriors (video game)") of the film in 2005.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-NYT2-14)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dan_Houser&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early work and Rockstar Games

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dan_Houser&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early work and Rockstar Games")]

In 1995, Houser got a part-time job at [BMG Interactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMG_Interactive "BMG Interactive") testing [CD-ROMs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CD-ROM "CD-ROM"); he became a full-time employee until 1996.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Meet_the_brains-10)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-15) Dan and Sam later became interested in a video game being developed by [DMA Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DMA_Design "DMA Design") called _Race'n'Chase_ after getting a preview of the game. The Housers signed _Race'n'Chase_ to BMG Interactive as the publisher and changed the name of the game to _[Grand Theft Auto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand\_Theft\_Auto\_(video\_game) "Grand Theft Auto (video game)")_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-16) Following the sale of BMG Interactive to [Take-Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take-Two "Take-Two") in 1998, Houser and his brother moved with the company to New York, where they founded Rockstar Games.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Meet_the_brains-10) He has cited the 3D _[Mario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario\_(franchise) "Mario (franchise)")_ and _[Zelda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda "The Legend of Zelda")_ games on the [Nintendo 64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_64 "Nintendo 64") as influences on his work.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-17)

Houser has been credited as a writer for twelve _Grand Theft Auto_ titles and a producer for six.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-18) Despite the high profile of the _Grand Theft Auto_ series, Houser and his brother have shied away from the celebrity spotlight, preferring to focus on the Rockstar Games brand rather than giving any one person the credit for the games' success.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-19) In 2009, both Dan and Sam Houser appeared in [_Time_ magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")'s [100 most influential people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100") of 2009 list.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-20)

Houser and his brother were inducted into the [Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Interactive_Arts_&_Sciences "Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences")'s Hall of Fame in 2014.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-21)

### Departure from Rockstar and founding of Absurd Ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dan_Houser&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Departure from Rockstar and founding of Absurd Ventures")]

In February 2020, Rockstar Games's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, announced Houser's resignation from Rockstar Games. He left Rockstar on 11 March 2020, following an extended break in 2019.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-23) In February 2021, Houser registered two companies in [Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware "Delaware"): [Absurd Ventures LLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absurd_Ventures_LLC "Absurd Ventures LLC") and Absurd Ventures in Games LLC, the latter with a UK-based subsidiary in [Altrincham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altrincham "Altrincham"). Houser is listed as the company's producer and creative director.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-VGC_Absurd-1) In June 2023, Houser officially announced his involvement in the studio, which he said will "create new universes" in video games, books, graphic novels, scripted podcasts, live-action, and animation.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-24)

In November 2023, it was revealed that [Lazlow Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazlow_Jones "Lazlow Jones") and Michael Unsworth had joined the company as executive producer and head of story, respectively.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-25) The company also announced its first projects: a graphic novel called _American Caper_ and an audio series called _A Better Paradise_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-26) In September 2024, Absurd Ventures announced the formation of Absurd Marin, made up of about 20 developers from [Ascendant Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascendant_Studios "Ascendant Studios"), developers of _[Immortals of Aveum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immortals\_of\_Aveum "Immortals of Aveum")_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-27)

In January 2025, Absurd Ventures released the logo and lineup of characters for the 'Absurdaverse', a new universe with animation and a "story-driven action-comedy adventure game."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-29)

Houser has novelised _A Better Paradise_ with the first volume published on October 14, 2025 accompanied by an audiobook edition on Audible.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-30)

In November 2025, Absurd Ventures began releasing a monthly comic book series titled _American Caper_, published by [Dark Horse Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_Horse_Comics "Dark Horse Comics"), with the first trade paperback collection scheduled for release in June 2026. [[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-31) A French edition was announced by publisher Urban Comics and scheduled for release in September 2026. [[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-32)

### Other work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dan_Houser&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Other work")]

By September 2022, Houser joined the advisory board of Revolving Games, a [blockchain game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain_game "Blockchain game") studio, after investing in a US$13.2 million funding round for the company;[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-VGC_Revolving-33) He met co-founder Saad Zaeem some years earlier to explore ideas, but they ultimately chose different projects, leading Houser to become an adviser and investor instead.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-VentureBeat_Revolving-34)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dan_Houser&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Houser is married to entrepreneur Krystyna Jakubiak.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Variety_LA-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Architectural_Digest-37) They previously lived in [Truman Capote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truman_Capote "Truman Capote")'s former home in the [Brooklyn Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Heights "Brooklyn Heights") neighborhood of New York City, which they purchased for US$12.5 million, the most expensive home sale in Brooklyn's history.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-40) In 2020, they purchased [Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien")'s former home in the [Brentwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brentwood,_Los_Angeles "Brentwood, Los Angeles") neighborhood of Los Angeles.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Variety_LA-36) They have three children and own a holiday lodge along [Saranac Lake, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saranac_Lake,_New_York "Saranac Lake, New York"), built in the 1920s.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Architectural_Digest-37) Houser holds both British and American citizenship.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-VGC_Absurd-1) Houser, Sam, and their wives were directors of the Houser Foundation Inc. in New York,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Foundation-41) founded in 2008; it was renamed the Krystyna and Dan Houser Foundation in 2024.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-42) Houser serves on the boards of the [Rainforest Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainforest_Alliance "Rainforest Alliance")[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-43) and [Brooklyn Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Museum "Brooklyn Museum").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-44)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Houser#cite_note-Foundation-41)
